body:
MEASURED ON HARDWARE 2026-08-23, Kobo Clara BW firmware 4.45.23792, against the
deployed server. This is the missing first link that makes F-3e383a and F-fed247
a live data-loss path rather than a theoretical one.

## The measured link

Bumping only `books.last_modified` -- exactly what
`cps/tasks/kepub_package_repair.py:332` does via
`mark_book_modified(..., set_dirty=False, unsync=False)` -- makes the device
**drop its downloaded copy of the book**.

On calibre book 446 (`1979 The Stories of John Cheever`, already downloaded, zero
annotations, chosen so nothing could be orphaned):

    v1/library/sync response   4009 B idle  ->  9066 B on the cycle after the bump
    requests carrying the uuid  ZERO across two complete sync cycles
    device IsDownloaded         true -> false
    device ___SyncTime          2026-08-18T00:18:34Z -> 2026-08-23T04:41:22Z
    device ___FileSize          unchanged
    books.timestamp / sort      unchanged (the repair does not touch them)

Control: across the same two device snapshots, of 229 ct6 books exactly one
changed `IsDownloaded` -- the bumped one. Downloaded count 6 -> 5. The only other
rows that moved were the two deleted `ZZ*` probe books, whose `___SyncTime` was
refreshed while staying `false`.

## Why that is the dangerous part

Section 6 of `notes/KOBO-HIGHLIGHTS-STATE.md` already measured, on a different
synced book, what a re-download does to annotations that already exist: the
`Bookmark` rows are KEPT, their `ContentID` is REWRITTEN to a bare
`OEBPS/<old filename>`, and they become invisible -- not drawn on the page, and
the book's Annotations panel reports "You don't have any annotations in this
book." The user cannot see them, jump to them, or delete them.

Composing the two:

    repair or backfill bumps last_modified
      -> device drops its downloaded copy              [OBSERVED, this finding]
      -> device re-downloads it later                  [ASSUMED, not observed]
      -> every pre-existing annotation is orphaned     [OBSERVED, section 6]
         silently, with no user-visible warning

So a maintenance task that is supposed to repair packaging can cost a reader
every highlight and bookmark in an affected book, and neither the task nor the
device says anything.

## Scope

Measured on the deployed library on 2026-08-18: 221 books, **11** with any live
annotation, 624 live annotations, three books holding 591 of them. Those 11 are
the exposed set; the ~210 annotation-free books can be repaired freely. That
matches the gating already recommended in section 6b -- gate on "this book has no
live annotation" and the risk is structurally absent rather than mitigated.

## What is NOT established

- The re-download step itself was not observed here; the book was left
  un-downloaded rather than reopened.
- Orphaning on re-download is OBSERVED, but on a different book in a previous
  session, and that book's package contents had also changed. Whether a
  byte-identical re-download orphans annotations is UNMEASURED.
- **Do not close that gap on the operator's real annotated books.** It needs a
  disposable synced book carrying disposable annotations.

## Suggested direction, not a decision

The cheap, safe fix is the gate, not a behaviour change: refuse to bump
`last_modified` for a book that has live annotations until writeback (F-3b565b)
can restore them, and say so in the task's report. Anything that re-delivers a
book to a device is annotation-affecting and should have to say what it will cost.
title: A last_modified bump makes a Kobo drop its downloaded copy, which turns any KEPUB repair into a silent annotation-orphaning path
